readme.html:
bc-word-layout-mcp

An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI agents create, edit, validate, and preview Microsoft Word report layouts for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central through deterministic, typed tools, instead of editing the OOXML by hand, where one misplaced element silently corrupts the document.

  • 30 typed MCP tools over stdio: inspect a layout and its dataset, author fields, labels, pictures, repeater tables and table structure, format text and cells, and refresh a layout after its dataset changes.
  • Every edit is validated before it is saved, and refused with the file untouched if it would corrupt the layout.
  • An offline mock PDF preview the agent can look at, and a dry-run merge that finds unresolved bindings.
  • One response shape for every tool, with an actionable hint on every error.

Install

The server reads and writes layout files with your permissions, at the paths the agent gives it. Point it only at repositories and layouts you trust, as you would any local build tool.

Plugin: the server and its skills (recommended)

The plugin installs the server together with four skills that teach an agent how to use it (see Skills). This repository is a plugin marketplace:

  • Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add TKapitan/bc-word-layout-mcp, then install the bc-word-layout plugin.
  • VS Code / GitHub Copilot (agent plugins, preview; Copilot CLI too): add "chat.plugins.marketplaces": ["TKapitan/bc-word-layout-mcp"] to your user settings.json, then install the bc-word-layout plugin.

NuGet package via dnx (needs the .NET 10 SDK)

dnx, part of the .NET 10 SDK, fetches and runs the server on demand.

VS Code (.vscode/mcp.json, or user-level mcp.json):

{
  "servers": {
    "bc-word-layout": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "dnx",
      "args": ["BcWordLayout.Mcp", "--yes"]
    }
  }
}

Claude Code (.mcp.json in a project):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bc-word-layout": {
      "command": "dnx",
      "args": ["BcWordLayout.Mcp", "--yes"]
    }
  }
}

or for your user: claude mcp add bc-word-layout -- dnx BcWordLayout.Mcp --yes.

Without a version, dnx runs the latest stable release. Pin one with BcWordLayout.Mcp@1.2.3; a pre-release runs only when pinned. dotnet tool install -g BcWordLayout.Mcp installs the same server as the bc-word-layout-mcp command instead.

Self-contained Windows binaries (no .NET needed)

Each GitHub Release has win-x64 and win-arm64 zips and an installer script that unpacks the latest one to %LOCALAPPDATA%\bc-word-layout-mcp\current\, verifies its checksum, and prints the config block to paste:

irm https://github.com/TKapitan/bc-word-layout-mcp/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex

For a specific version, run that release's own script with -Version:

& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://github.com/TKapitan/bc-word-layout-mcp/releases/download/v1.2.3/install.ps1))) -Version 1.2.3

To run the server from a clone of this repository, see CONTRIBUTING.md.

Skills

The server works on its own, but agents use it noticeably better with its skills. The plugin installs them; without it, copy the folders under skills/ into your project's .claude/skills/ or .github/skills/ (or your user-level ~/.claude/skills/).

  • al-word-layout: the intended workflow (inspect → edit → validate → preview → sandbox verify), the full tool reference, and the error codes.
  • al-word-layout-design: what a new layout should look like, from Business Central's own document conventions.
  • al-word-layout-from-design: from a finished Word design and the report's empty layout to a bound layout.
  • al-word-layout-composite: composable layouts, meaning the report body, a reusable header/footer layout, and a report theme.

Requirements

  • Windows (x64 or arm64). Linux and macOS are not supported yet.
  • Microsoft Word is optional. preview_layout uses it to turn the merged mock into a PDF. Without it, the preview still returns the merged .docx and says why there is no PDF; every other tool works without Word.

Configuration

Target Business Central version

Some layout features need a newer Business Central. Each call works out the target, the minimum BC version the layout must work on; the first match wins:

  1. The nearest AL app.json above the layout (above outputPath for create_layout): its application, e.g. 29.0.0.0. The search stops at a folder containing .git.
  2. BCWL_BC_VERSION (e.g. 29 or 29.1) in the server's env block, for layouts outside an AL project.
  3. Otherwise the target is unknown.

get_layout_info and validate_layout report the target they used. A tool that would write a feature from the table below refuses with bc_version_unsupported when the target is lower or unknown, and validate_layout reports such a feature a layout already has. The gated features are:

  • theme colours such as accent1 (in format.color, fill and borderColor);
  • paragraphStyle;
  • set_layout_theme.

Hex colours are never gated.

Feature Kind Since Covers Evidence
report-themes capability 29.0 report theme .dotx files, header/footer layouts bound to Tenant_Report_Defaults 2026 release wave 2; a composite body + header/footer + theme set printed on 2026-10-17
themable-formatting capability 29.0 theme-slot colours for text, cell fills and borders, paragraph styles, and the layout's own theme colours and fonts decided with report themes, 2026-10-27 (#152)

Label columns

The tools treat a dataset column as a label when its name ends in Lbl/_Lbl, and every column of a data item named Labels. Two environment variables change that:

  • BCWL_LABEL_SUFFIXES: comma-separated label suffixes, e.g. Lbl,Caption (default Lbl).
  • BCWL_LABELS_DATA_ITEM: the labels data item's name, or - to turn that rule off (default Labels).
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bc-word-layout": {
      "command": "dnx",
      "args": ["BcWordLayout.Mcp", "--yes"],
      "env": { "BCWL_BC_VERSION": "29", "BCWL_LABEL_SUFFIXES": "Lbl,Caption" }
    }
  }
}

Tools

Tool Purpose
get_layout_info Inspect a layout: report identity, every content control, header/footer parts, every table's rows and cells (with the coordinates the cell and column tools take), the target BC version, and its look (theme, colours, styles).
list_dataset_fields List the dataset (data items and columns) from a layout or a schema .xml, marking labels and, for a layout, which columns are bound.
validate_layout Check structure and bindings (level=quick), or also dry-run merge sample data so every unresolved binding becomes a finding (level=full).
preview_layout Merge sample (or real) data into a copy of the layout and convert it to PDF: a mock preview.
render_preview_pages Return pages of a preview PDF as images the agent can look at, optionally also saved as .png files.
create_layout Create a new layout from a report schema, blank or over a branded template; theme: "office" adds the stock Office theme.
insert_field Insert a field bound to a dataset column, in the body, a header or a footer.
insert_label Insert a label bound to a caption column.
insert_text Insert static text, such as the separator between two fields.
insert_page_number Insert "Page X / Y" (or just X).
insert_page_conditional_text Insert text that prints on the last page only, every page but the last, or the first page only.
insert_repeater_table Insert a line-items table that repeats per record, in the Business Central look by default.
insert_repeater_row Add a detail row under each line of an existing repeater (assembly components, serial numbers).
insert_picture Insert a picture bound to a dataset column, such as the company logo.
insert_table Insert a plain table, in the body, a header or a footer: address blocks, caption/value grids, totals blocks.
wrap_in_repeater Make existing content repeat per record, e.g. one page per customer in a statement.
remove_control Remove a content control by its id, optionally keeping its content.
set_cell_text Replace the plain text of a table cell.
set_text_format Restyle text already in the layout: bold, italic, underline, size, font, colour, styles, alignment.
set_layout_theme Change the layout's own theme colours and fonts; everything coloured through the theme follows.
clear_cell_text Remove the plain text from a table cell.
insert_subtotal_row Add a row after each group of a repeater, for subtotals or spacing.
insert_table_row Insert a row that prints once, such as a totals row inside the lines table.
set_column_widths Set a table's column widths.
insert_column Add a column at any position, bound or plain; the table keeps its width.
remove_column Remove a column.
merge_cells Merge adjacent cells of one row.
split_cells Split a merged cell back into single cells.
set_cell_format Draw cell borders (rules) in any colour and fill cells.
refresh_xml_part Update a layout to a changed report dataset, reporting bindings that no longer resolve and new fields.

The al-word-layout skill documents every parameter.

Responses and errors

Every tool returns the same envelope:

{ "ok": true, "data": { "...": "tool-specific payload" } }

On failure, ok is false and error carries { code, message, hint }. The hint always names the next step, such as which argument to fix or which tool to call first. Malformed calls (an unknown tool or argument, a wrong type, a relative path) get the same envelope. render_preview_pages adds one image per page after the envelope.

The 24 mutating tools (insert_field, insert_label, insert_text, insert_page_number, insert_page_conditional_text, insert_picture, insert_table, insert_repeater_table, insert_repeater_row, insert_subtotal_row, insert_table_row, wrap_in_repeater, remove_control, set_cell_text, set_text_format, set_layout_theme, clear_cell_text, set_column_widths, insert_column, remove_column, merge_cells, split_cells, set_cell_format, refresh_xml_part) validate every edit before saving it:

  • An edit that would corrupt the file or break a table is refused (edit_would_corrupt, edit_would_break_table), and the file on disk is left untouched.
  • A successful edit returns a fresh quickValidation summary.
  • Every save removes a link to an external Word template, which Business Central refuses to upload.

Preview and Business Central

preview_layout merges sample data (or a real dataset you export from BC, via dataOverridesPath) into a copy of the layout and converts it to PDF offline. It never runs the real Business Central report engine.

  • What it is good for: catching structural and binding mistakes on every edit.
  • What can differ from BC: captions, fonts and exact pagination.
  • Data it can't reproduce: sample data fills every field, and the preview ignores the Word add-in's hide-if-empty controls.

Final sign-off on a layout is always a Business Central sandbox render.

Layouts made with these tools have been printed in BC 28 and BC 29 sandboxes (Cronus AU): BC accepts them, bindings resolve, repeaters expand, and the preview's structure matched the real render. docs/FIDELITY-CHECKLIST.md records every round.

Not supported

  • The Word add-in's conditional controls (Hide Table Row If Empty, Hide Field If Zero, Hide Table Column If Empty, layout comments): no tool writes them yet. Their Business Central behaviour is measured in #123 and #162; until then, edit them by hand.
  • Repeaters in headers and footers. Nothing shows that BC prints them, so the tools create repeaters only in the body.
  • Margins, page setup, and defining new styles. Start from a branded template (create_layout's templatePath), or edit in Word and run validate_layout afterwards.
  • Report theme .dotx files: set_layout_theme changes a layout's own theme only. A report theme selected in BC replaces the layout's own theme when it prints.
  • Creating a vertical cell merge. Tables that already have merges can be edited.
  • Generating the dataset schema. It always comes from Business Central: a layout the AL compiler generated, an exported layout, or an exported schema .xml (ADR-0006). A new layout starts with one AL build or one export.
  • Translated captions in the preview. Pass a real exported dataset for real captions.
  • RDL and Excel layouts, and uploading a layout to Business Central.

Public contract and versioning

Semantic versioning. The public API is the tool names, their parameters, the {ok, data, error} envelope and the error codes. Removing or changing any of them happens only in a major release; new tools, optional parameters, fields and error codes come in minor ones. Error message and hint texts can change at any time, so never parse them.

  • Business Central: validated on BC 28 and BC 29. Word report layouts are a long-stable format, so other versions are expected to work; reports are welcome.
  • MCP SDK: an exact version of the official C# SDK, upgraded in minor releases, with any change in behaviour noted in the changelog.

More

  • CHANGELOG.md: release notes.
  • GitHub issues: what is planned or deferred, and why.
  • docs/SOLUTION-DESIGN.md and docs/adr/: architecture and design decisions.
  • CONTRIBUTING.md: building from source and contributing.
  • SECURITY.md: reporting a vulnerability.
